title: TERRA BELLUM
tagline: A turn-based chronicle of the globe
pick_nation: Tap a province to claim its nation
err_needport: A port is needed to cross the sea
mp_pick_hint: Tap a province to claim its nation
tut_1_b: You rule a nation of provinces under a named ruler. Tap a province to inspect it. The ribbon on top shows gold, manpower, move points, diplomacy points and intel; the dock on the left opens every screen.
tut_2_b: Recruit troops in your provinces, then press Move army and tap a neighbouring province. Moving into enemy land attacks it; you can also right-click a target. Neutral land is claimed by Colonize.
tut_3_b: Declare war from a nation card or a province. Occupy enemy provinces to raise your war score, then demand land or white peace. Long occupations annex provinces.
tut_4_b: Build farms, markets and libraries. The Budget screen sets taxes, public goods, research and investment. Research unlocks eras; gold can also hire mercenaries.
tut_5_b: Open Nations to see rulers, relations and casus belli. War without a reason raises infamy; at 22 the world forms a coalition against you. Sign trade deals with friends for steady gold.
tut_6_b: Decrees spend gold for lasting bonuses. Historical and random events ask for decisions with real consequences, and your ruler will age and be succeeded.

blurb_modern: The world as it stands: nuclear powers, shifting alliances, hundreds of nations.
blurb_ancient: Rome and Carthage clash as Qin unifies China. Phalanxes, war elephants, tribal kings.
blurb_roman: Hadrian's Rome at its greatest extent, facing Parthia across the Euphrates.
blurb_medieval: The First Crusade marches. Feudal kingdoms, caliphates and steppe confederations.
blurb_mongol: The Mongol khanates hold the largest land empire in history.
blurb_timurid: Timur's armies tear across Asia while the Ottomans rise in the west.
blurb_discovery: Columbus sails. Spain, Portugal and the Ottomans begin to reshape the world.
blurb_gunpowder: Musket and cannon empires: Louis XIV, Peter the Great, Aurangzeb.
blurb_napoleonic: Napoleon bestrides Europe while the old empires gather against him.
blurb_victorian: Steam, rails and colonies. The Great Powers carve up the globe.
blurb_ww1: Alliances lock Europe into a war nobody can stop. Trenches, machine guns, empires.
blurb_ww2: Fascism, communism and democracy collide in the largest war ever fought.
blurb_coldwar: Two superpowers, a nuclear shadow, and a world dividing into blocs.

tut_7_b: The Advisor flags crises and good opportunities, and the Annals record your history. Win by domination, wealth, technology, diplomacy or conquest (Goals). Press the seal to end the turn: each turn is six months.

codex_infamy_b: Starting a war without a casus belli adds 8 infamy, taking land adds more. Infamy fades slowly. At 22 the world forms a coalition against you and every nation gains a casus belli on you until infamy falls below 12.
codex_cb_b: A reason for war costs no infamy: reclaiming your old provinces, revenge for a grudge, helping an ally, suppressing rebels, joining a coalition, or an ultimatum that was refused.
codex_ultimatum_b: From a border province of a nation at peace with you, demand it without war (2 diplomacy points). A weaker ruler yields; otherwise war follows with a free casus belli. AI rulers yield when you are about 2.4 times stronger.
codex_generals_b: Appoint a commander to an army of 12 or more. Each star adds 6% strength to the army he leads; victories earn stars, defeats may kill him. He rides with the column when the whole stack moves. Bigger realms and martial rulers field more.
codex_supply_b: A province feeds only so many soldiers. Armies above the limit in foreign land lose 7% of the excess every turn. Development, farms and supply camps raise the limit; mountains and marsh cut it.
codex_rulers_b: Every nation has a named ruler with administration, diplomacy and military skills and a trait. Hereditary realms may suffer a succession crisis; republics hold elections. A royal marriage can bind two realms or even join them in a personal union.
codex_trade_b: Trade deals pay both partners gold every turn; the number of deals grows with your era. Decrees spend gold for lasting bonuses such as military reform or patronage of scholars.
codex_realms_b: Hold most of a historic region such as Iberia or the Nile Valley to unify it for a lasting reward. The Goals screen shows the nearest ones.
codex_victory_b: Dominate 25% of the world, hoard 5,000 gold, reach technology 5.0, hold eight alliances, or be the last nation standing. Honours on the title screen record your feats across games.
hot_hint: Several people share this device and take their turns in order. Pass it on when the screen asks.
al_no_general: A commander would strengthen your biggest army. Appoint a general from the command card.
al_ult_chance: A neighbour at peace is {r}x weaker than you: an ultimatum may win this province without a war.
doctrine_hint: A lasting stance for the whole realm. Adopting costs 2 diplomacy points, changing it {c}.
codex_doctrine_b: Adopt a martial, mercantile or administrative doctrine from the Decisions screen (2 diplomacy points, 4 to change). Each gives a steady bonus: army strength and manpower, gold, or cheaper administration and faster research.
pv_win: Victory: {k} of your men hold the province (you lose {l}).
pv_lose: Defeat: you would lose {a}, they would lose {d}.
codex_battle_b: Combat is deterministic: your force times era, terrain, ruler and general bonuses against the defenders times terrain, fortress and general. Choosing an attack shows the exact outcome before you commit. The Send control on your province sends 25 to 100 percent of the stack.
